concepts.description: System 2 adjusts insufficiently away from an anchor, stopping at the edge of uncertainty nearest the starting point.
concepts.title: Adjust-and-Anchor Heuristic

concepts.description: Opposing experts jointly design scorable forecast questions under shared rules — many precise bets and clusters beat polemic that never updates on outcomes.
concepts.title: Adversarial Collaboration for Forecasts

concepts.description: Letting likes and dislikes drive beliefs about benefits and risks when conclusions dominate over arguments.
concepts.title: Affect Heuristic

concepts.description: Choices violating expected utility theory by overweighting certainty relative to small probability improvements.
concepts.title: Allais Paradox

concepts.description: Anchors selectively evoke compatible associative evidence in System 1, biasing retrieval before System 2 estimates.
concepts.title: Anchoring as Priming

concepts.description: Estimates stay near a previously considered number even when that number is arbitrary or uninformative.
concepts.title: Anchoring Effect

concepts.description: System 1 spreads activation across ideas, emotions, and body responses into self-reinforcing coherent patterns that feel like understanding.
concepts.title: Associative Coherence and Activation

concepts.description: System 1 automatically links events into causal narratives for coherence, often post-hoc and regardless of actual causation.
concepts.title: Automatic Causal Storytelling

concepts.description: Media-driven self-reinforcing cycles that make minor risks feel important and reset policy priorities through escalating public concern.
concepts.title: Availability Cascade

concepts.description: Judging likelihood by how easily examples come to mind — a System 1 shortcut that ignores evidence quality and base rates.
concepts.title: Availability Heuristic

concepts.description: Overweighting case-specific information and underweighting population base rates when judging probabilities, even when base rates are known.
concepts.title: Base Rate Neglect

concepts.description: Combining prior base-rate beliefs with diagnostic evidence via Bayes's rule to reach calibrated posterior probabilities.
concepts.title: Bayesian Updating with Base Rates

concepts.description: Tenacious resistance to revising beliefs tied to identity or public commitment, a major driver of underreaction in forecasting.
concepts.title: Belief Perseverance and Identity-Protective Cognition

concepts.description: Utility-of-wealth models fail because happiness depends on changes relative to reference points, not absolute wealth states alone.
concepts.title: Bernoulli's Error

concepts.description: Radically improbable consequential events resist skill measurement and may dominate history — but many consequences and modest tail risks remain forecastable.
concepts.title: Black Swan Forecast Limits

concepts.description: A proper scoring rule measuring distance between forecast probability and outcome — lower is better, like golf.
concepts.title: Brier Score

concepts.description: Calibration asks whether stated probabilities match frequencies; resolution asks whether forecasts sort outcomes decisively away from 50%.
concepts.title: Calibration vs Resolution

concepts.description: Practices with science's outward form but without systematic doubt and testing produce confident error — as in pre-RCT medicine and untested forecasting methods.
concepts.title: Cargo Cult Science and Doubt

concepts.description: Shared category norms specify both typical values and the range of plausible variation — letting language communicate efficiently without literal violations.
concepts.title: Categorical Norms and Plausible Ranges

concepts.description: Population statistics used only when they fit a causal story about the case; otherwise neglected in favor of case-specific narrative.
concepts.title: Causal Versus Statistical Base Rates

concepts.description: Rare events are overweighted when prospects are described verbally but often underweighted when learned only through repeated sampling without the rare draw.
concepts.title: Choice from Experience vs Description

concepts.description: A System 1 dial from Easy to Strained whose causes and consequences swap — fluency, mood, truth illusions, and intuition load on one interchangeable network.
concepts.title: Cognitive Ease

concepts.description: Pupil dilation tracks the current rate of mental-energy use — peaking during demanding transformations and staying small during routine conversation.
concepts.title: Cognitive Pupillometry and Mental Effort

concepts.description: Forecasters focus on their own plan and capabilities while neglecting rivals' actions, producing excess entry and overestimated control.
concepts.title: Competition Neglect

concepts.description: System 1 tends to believe by default; System 2 must actively doubt — and is often busy, lazy, or confirmatory in hypothesis testing.
concepts.title: Confirmation Bias and System 1 Gullibility

concepts.description: Judging a conjunction of events more probable than one of its constituents when a richer story feels more representative.
concepts.title: Conjunction Fallacy

concepts.description: Focusing on numerators or vivid cases while ignoring the base population size that sets the true rate.
concepts.title: Denominator Neglect

concepts.description: Irrelevant information dilutes confidence in stereotype-consistent judgments even when it should be ignored — an overreaction failure mode.
concepts.title: Dilution Effect

concepts.description: Synthesizing many clashing causal perspectives into one forecast rather than defaulting to a single dove or hawk frame.
concepts.title: Dragonfly Eye Perspective Aggregation

concepts.description: During peak mental effort, System 2 protects the priority task and can render people effectively blind to concurrent stimuli — selective overload, not blackout.
concepts.title: Effort Narrows Attention

concepts.description: Self-control and deliberate thought draw on a limited shared pool of mental effort — depletion weakens judgment and self-control sequentially.
concepts.title: Ego Depletion and Mental Effort Budget

concepts.description: Owning a good for use raises its subjective value relative to not owning it, because giving up feels like a loss weighted more than acquiring feels like a gain.
concepts.title: Endowment Effect

concepts.description: System 2 adopts task sets that override habitual responses — switching sets and holding multiple tagged items are among the most effortful cognitive work.
concepts.title: Executive Control and Task Sets

concepts.description: Post-aggregation adjustment pushing crowd estimates toward 0 or 1 when judges hold diverse, non-overlapping information — ineffective when diversity is zero.
concepts.title: Extremizing Algorithm

concepts.description: Voters substitute fast face-based competence impressions for the harder question of actual job performance — with larger effect for uninformed viewers.
concepts.title: Facial Competence Heuristic

concepts.description: Even in regular environments, expertise depends on fast clear feedback and adequate practice — and miniskills vary within a domain.
concepts.title: Feedback Quality and Skill Acquisition

concepts.description: Breaking intractable estimates into tractable sub-problems with explicit assumptions — flushing ignorance into the open.
concepts.title: Fermi Decomposition

concepts.description: Whatever you attend to looms large in global evaluation — "nothing in life is as important as you think it is when you are thinking about it."
concepts.title: Focusing Illusion

concepts.description: Judging forecasters by process compliance without scoring outcomes repeats medicine's pre-evidence error — accuracy must be measured to improve.
concepts.title: Forecast Accuracy Accountability

concepts.description: Empirical ordering from GJP tournaments — superteams beat prediction markets, which beat ordinary teams, which beat wisdom-of-crowd averages of solos.
concepts.title: Forecast Aggregation Hierarchy

concepts.description: Unflinching review of forecast failures and successes to separate luck from reasoning quality.
concepts.title: Forecast Postmortem

concepts.description: Focus forecasting effort on questions in a Goldilocks zone — neither clocklike nor hopelessly cloudlike.
concepts.title: Forecastability Triage

concepts.description: Prospect theory's 2×2 of gains/losses and high/low probability predicts when people accept or reject gambles — including desperate risk seeking on bad options.
concepts.title: Fourfold Pattern of Risk Attitudes

concepts.description: Equivalent outcomes described differently shift choices because reference points and decision weights respond to presentation, not just facts.
concepts.title: Framing Effects

concepts.description: Presenting probabilities as frequencies over explicit individuals makes subset relations obvious and reduces conjunction and denominator neglect errors.
concepts.title: Frequency Format Framing

concepts.description: System 1 pools experiences into character impressions unless a rare event is vivid enough to be recalled separately — explaining when rare events are neglected.
concepts.title: Global Impressions vs Explicit Gambles

concepts.description: Short-term targets become reference points where falling short feels like loss and exceeding feels like gain — distorting effort and economic logic.
concepts.title: Goals as Reference Points

concepts.description: Frequent small probability revisions proportional to diagnostic weight of new evidence — the Bayesian spirit without necessarily crunching the formula.
concepts.title: Granular Bayesian Updating

concepts.description: Small cohesive groups maintain esprit by shared illusions that suppress critical testing — cured by structured dissent, not just adding smart people.
concepts.title: Groupthink in Forecasting Teams

concepts.description: Deliberate debiasing techniques absorbed into automatic habit through practice, lightening cognitive load without eliminating fragility.
concepts.title: Habituated System 2

concepts.description: A global impression of one trait spills over to unrelated judgments, driven by associative coherence.
concepts.title: Halo Effect

concepts.description: Tetlock's typology — single-big-idea hedgehogs versus multi-causal foxes — predicting who forecasts political events better (still poorly).
concepts.title: Hedgehogs Versus Foxes

concepts.description: Diagnostic labels for predictable judgment errors — shared vocabulary lets agents locate, anticipate, and challenge unreliable intuitions.
concepts.title: Heuristics and Biases Vocabulary

concepts.description: Complex geopolitical forecasting retains a large role for judgment, but validated algorithms and AI should augment humans where they exist — not replace measured hybrid teams.
concepts.title: Human-Machine Forecasting Hybrid

concepts.description: Subjective confidence and coherence in prediction often exceed what the environment's predictability actually supports.
concepts.title: Illusion of Validity and Skill

concepts.description: Collect private estimates before group talk to decorrelate errors and preserve diverse information — wisdom-of-crowds prerequisite.
concepts.title: Independent Judgments Before Discussion

concepts.description: Forecasting from case-specific plans versus anchoring on base rates from a reference class of similar cases.
concepts.title: Inside View vs Outside View

concepts.description: Expert intuition is associative recognition — a cue triggers stored patterns and the answer feels immediate, not mysterious.
concepts.title: Intuition as Recognition

concepts.description: System 1 delivers fast, confident intuitive answers whether they come from skill or heuristics, with no built-in warning when they are unreliable.
concepts.title: Intuition Without a Reliability Signal

concepts.description: Forecast accuracy often loses to power and tribal interest — accuracy is welcomed only when convenient unless institutions commit to scorekeeping.
concepts.title: Kto-Kogo and Forecast Adoption Obstacles

concepts.description: Given several ways to achieve the same goal, people gravitate to the least demanding — effort is a cost in the economy of action.
concepts.title: Law of Least Effort

concepts.description: The intuition that small samples are as representative as large ones — leading to overconfidence in extreme results from small N.
concepts.title: Law of Small Numbers

concepts.description: System 2 often fails to monitor System 1 not from incapacity but insufficient motivation — a distinct failure mode from raw intelligence.
concepts.title: Lazy System 2 and Rationality

concepts.description: Adding detail or items can increase perceived probability or value in single evaluation because System 1 averages instead of adding.
concepts.title: Less Is More Pattern

concepts.description: Outcomes evaluated as gains or losses relative to a reference point, with losses weighted more heavily than equal gains — core of prospect theory.
concepts.title: Loss Aversion and Reference Points

concepts.description: In low-validity environments, simple statistical formulas consistently match or beat clinical judgment — with no documented exception across decades of research.
concepts.title: Meehl Clinical vs Statistical Prediction

concepts.description: Informal accounts that organize money and outcomes into separate buckets, often distorting rational comprehensive evaluation.
concepts.title: Mental Accounting

concepts.description: A question-acceptance error where an incongruous detail goes unnoticed because it is not abnormal within the activated context — norm theory in action.
concepts.title: Moses Illusion

concepts.description: Miles-per-gallon framing misleads fuel-saving comparisons because mpg is nonlinear in gallons consumed — gallons-per-mile is the rational frame.
concepts.title: MPG Illusion

concepts.description: Constructing tidy causal stories from sparse evidence, overweighting coherence over statistical support.
concepts.title: Narrative Fallacy

concepts.description: Bad news, threats, and losses receive priority processing over good news — the broader psychology behind loss aversion.
concepts.title: Negativity Dominance

concepts.description: System 1 maintains an associative model of what is normal; surprise flags violated expectations and single incidents can retroactively rewrite norms.
concepts.title: Norm Theory and Surprise

concepts.description: Systematic overestimation of favorable outcomes, personal attributes, and controllability — often the most decision-consequential cognitive bias.
concepts.title: Optimistic Bias

concepts.description: Tetlock's synthesis — expert forecasting is often poor on long-horizon complex questions, yet measurable skill exists in pockets when accuracy is tracked.
concepts.title: Optimistic Skeptic Stance

concepts.description: Judging decisions by outcomes rather than the quality of the decision at the time, corrupting forecast feedback.
concepts.title: Outcome Bias and Hindsight

concepts.description: Probability judgments for rare focal events inflate when alternatives are diffuse, driven by confirmatory retrieval and cognitive ease of plausible scenarios.
concepts.title: Overestimation of Unlikely Events

concepts.description: Treating forecasts and beliefs as continually tested drafts rather than final releases, driving the strongest gains in forecasting skill.
concepts.title: Perpetual Beta

concepts.description: Plans and forecasts unrealistically close to best-case scenarios that would improve by consulting statistics of similar cases.
concepts.title: Planning Fallacy

concepts.description: Decision weights overweight improbable outcomes and underweight near-certain ones relative to their true probabilities.
concepts.title: Possibility and Certainty Effects

concepts.description: Helping others clarify arguments so they aren't misunderstood — a team epistemic skill for better-calibrated collective judgment.
concepts.title: Precision Questioning

concepts.description: Before committing to a plan, imagine it failed and write the disaster history — a debiasing ritual against groupthink and uncritical optimism.
concepts.title: Premortem Technique

concepts.description: Finer numeric probability distinctions improve forecast accuracy — rounding superforecaster estimates measurably hurts performance.
concepts.title: Probabilistic Forecast Granularity

concepts.description: Small risks are either ignored entirely or overweighted with little sensitivity to actual probability — the numerator story dominates the denominator.
concepts.title: Probability Neglect

concepts.description: Following a rigorous discovery or design process does not guarantee good outcomes — skill, focus, and calibration checks remain separate.
concepts.title: Process-Skill Decoupling

concepts.description: Most shipped software features and product bets land in a mediocre middle — reference-class statistics for calibrating discovery and build optimism.
concepts.title: Product Build Outcome Base Rates

concepts.description: People transform objective probabilities into decision weights that diverge from linear probability — the core of prospect theory's descriptive model.
concepts.title: Prospect Theory Decision Weights

concepts.description: Prospect theory treats "win nothing" as zero value at the reference point in all contexts, but high-probability large wins make zero intensely disappointing.
concepts.title: Prospect Theory Disappointment Limit

concepts.description: System 1 represents categories by prototypes or typical exemplars, so it handles averages well but neglects quantity when judging sum-like variables.
concepts.title: Prototype vs Sum Representation

concepts.description: Unscorable big-picture questions decompose into many small scorable forecasts whose Bayesian-style updates collectively answer what pundits leave vague.
concepts.title: Question Clustering for Big Questions

concepts.description: Outside-view method that anchors on distributional statistics from similar past cases before adjusting for case-specific factors.
concepts.title: Reference Class Forecasting

concepts.description: Shrink nonregressive System 1 forecasts toward the category mean in proportion to evidence-outcome correlation.
concepts.title: Regression-Corrected Intuitive Prediction

concepts.description: Extreme observations tend toward the average on retest because luck and sampling variance do not persist — often mistaken for causation.
concepts.title: Regression to the Mean

concepts.description: Identical outcomes trigger stronger regret and blame when produced by action or deviation from default than when produced by inaction or staying with default.
concepts.title: Regret and Action-Inaction Asymmetry

concepts.description: Judging probability or likelihood by how much an instance resembles a stereotype, often substituting similarity for statistical reasoning.
concepts.title: Representativeness Heuristic

concepts.description: People demand far more to accept a risk they actively choose than to pay to prevent the same risk — responsibility for bad outcomes amplifies loss aversion.
concepts.title: Responsibility Aversion Beyond Loss Aversion

concepts.description: Standing rules that embed single risky choices in a class of similar choices, correcting narrow framing, optimism, and loss aversion.
concepts.title: Risk Policies and Broad Framing

concepts.description: Probability estimates must vary with time horizon and question scope — a bias where people give the same answer regardless of scale.
concepts.title: Scope Sensitivity

concepts.description: Vague verbal probability terms hide disagreement; numeric ranges force metacognition and make forecasts testable.
concepts.title: Sherman Kent Probability Language

concepts.description: Equal-weight linear formulas and checklists often outperform expert judgment in low-validity environments because they are simpler and more consistent.
concepts.title: Simple Models Beating Expert Judgment

concepts.description: Judgments made in isolation often diverge from comparative evaluation because System 1 responds to salient emotions and anchors invisible in side-by-side view.
concepts.title: Single Versus Joint Evaluation

concepts.description: Biases resist direct correction of intuitive thinking; the main achievable progress is recognizing situations where errors are likely and slowing down.
concepts.title: Situational Bias Recognition

concepts.description: Persistence of individual differences in achievement distinguishes skill from luck in forecasting and trading domains.
concepts.title: Skill vs Luck Diagnosis

concepts.description: Answering an easier question in place of the one actually asked when the target question is too difficult for automatic judgment.
concepts.title: Substitution Heuristic

concepts.description: Continuing to invest in a losing course because prior costs feel unredeemed, ignoring better forward-looking options.
concepts.title: Sunk-Cost Fallacy

concepts.description: Broad-brush modal traits of top tournament forecasters — outlook, methods, and work ethic — not a checklist every expert must match.
concepts.title: Superforecaster Composite Profile

concepts.description: Asking the right unscorable question and answering scorable ones well are complementary skills — often carried by different psychological profiles.
concepts.title: Superquestioner Versus Superforecaster

concepts.description: How elite forecast teams combine psychological safety, active open-mindedness, and generous information sharing to beat solo work without groupthink.
concepts.title: Superteam Forecasting Dynamics

concepts.description: Dual-process frame — fast automatic System 1 versus effortful analytical System 2 — for locating where a judgment came from and why it may fail.
concepts.title: System 1 and System 2

concepts.description: Intuitive forecasting collapses uncertainty into gonna-happen, not-gonna-happen, or maybe — coarse settings that undermine calibration until subdivided numerically.
concepts.title: Three-Setting Probability Dial

concepts.description: Evaluating dimensions independently before combining judgments reduces halo effect and associative coherence bias.
concepts.title: Trait-by-Trait Scoring

concepts.description: Expert intuition is likely valid only when the environment is sufficiently regular and the judge had prolonged practice learning its regularities.
concepts.title: Two Conditions for Trustworthy Expert Intuition

concepts.description: Rich mental representations of outcomes — emotional or not — shrink the role probability plays in valuation relative to expected-value calculation.
concepts.title: Vivid Outcomes Reduce Probability Sensitivity

concepts.description: Environments where feedback misleads learning or valid cues are too weak for reliable intuitive forecasting, even for genuine experts.
concepts.title: Wicked and Low-Validity Environments

concepts.description: Averaging many independent estimates cancels random error and accumulates dispersed signal — but quality depends on diversity and knowledge.
concepts.title: Wisdom of Crowds in Forecasting

concepts.description: Judging probabilistic forecasts by which side of 50% they fell on rather than whether the stated probability was well-calibrated.
concepts.title: Wrong Side of Maybe Fallacy

concepts.description: What You See Is All There Is — the tendency to construct coherent stories from available evidence without accounting for what is missing or uncertain.
concepts.title: WYSIATI
